STEP 1 - Scene: A light snack or side. Two cut pieces of corn on the cob sit on a white plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish side/dinner plate about 24 cm across. Its area is roughly 24² × 0.85 ≈ 490 cm² (rounded square), call it 450 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: two corn cob segments (cooked sweet corn on the cob). No visible oil or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: Each piece is about 100 px across in a plate about 345 px wide, which is 24 × 100/345 ≈ 7 cm. Each cross-section is 3.14 × 3.5² ≈ 38 cm². Two pieces give about 76 cm², or ~17% of the plate. The total covered share is 17%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each piece lies as a short cylinder about 3 cm tall (seen end-on). Volume per piece ≈ 38 × 3 ≈ 115 ml, so two pieces ≈ 230 ml. The diameter is probably a bit overestimated, since the cobs look about 6 cm wide. Using 6 cm: area 28 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 85 ml each, so ≈ 170 ml for both.

STEP 6 - Grams: The cob includes the core, and the density is about 0.65 g/ml, so 170 × 0.65 ≈ 110 g. A 3 cm cob segment with a 6 cm diameter would weigh about 55 g, which is plausible.

STEP 7 - Energy: Corn on the cob is about 96 kcal/100 g, so 110 g gives ≈ 106 kcal. The cob is partly inedible, but the estimate covers the visible food.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two small corn pieces weighing about 110 g and about 105 kcal is reasonable.
